<a id="cloudflare-dns-token"></a>

## cloudflare.dns-token

All-domains DNS token used by the pinned CLI, hosting helper, and hosted MCP.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `~/.agents/local/credentials/cloudflare.env`.

Variable names: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`.

Declared permissions: `Zone: DNS Edit for all zones`, `Zone: Zone Read for all zones`, `User: User Details Read`.

Consumers: `cloudflare.cli`, `cloudflare.mcp`, `hosting.paul`.

Provider label: Agent DNS — all domains. Scope was user-authorized and verified on 2026-10-14; use check --live to establish current access.

The profile is ignored, owner-only mode 600, in an owner-only mode-700 directory. No token value belongs in this inventory.

The profile also contains the non-secret account selector. The default zone is deliberately unbound; project manifests choose their zone.

Permissions are the dashboard-confirmed declared grant. Read-only checks prove token/user/zone/DNS reads, not DNS Edit or all-zone grants. The deprecated zone.permissions field is not API-token introspection.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/cloudflare-token.md).

<a id="railway-workspace-token"></a>

## railway.workspace-token

Railway workspace API token for all workspace projects, read from the shell secrets file.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `~/.secrets.sh`.

Variable names: `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`.

Declared permissions: `Workspace c64d0999-e00c-4c52-bbd4-2614210e3758 (my workspace); do not infer scope from account identity endpoint failures`.

Consumers: `railway.mcp`, `hosting.paul`.

Tools read only the literal RAILWAY_API_TOKEN assignment from ~/.secrets.sh and never execute the file. Shells export the same value; see shell.secrets.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/railway.md).

<a id="shell-secrets"></a>

## shell.secrets

Global shell secret file loaded by normal zsh and login/interactive Bash on this machine.

Owner: **reference**.

Location: `~/.secrets.sh`.

Variable names: `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`, `PARALLEL_API_KEY`.

~/.zshenv loads it for normal zsh; ~/.profile and ~/.bashrc load it for login/interactive Bash. Children inherit exports. Clean noninteractive Bash does not load these files and needs explicit injection or the registered profile loader. ~/.shortcuts.sh contains aliases/directory helpers, not Railway credentials or target selection.

It is a shell script with other credentials and commands. Profiles registered with variables read only those literal assignments; never execute it from tools or print its lines. Authorized edits must preserve unrelated assignments.

App-local .env files use their own loaders; see environment.project-secrets. Cloud agents do not have this file; inject secrets through each platform's secret manager.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/configuration.md).

<a id="environment-cloudflare"></a>

## environment.cloudflare

Cloudflare authentication and target selector variable names.

Owner: **agents**.

Variable names: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID`.

CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is secret. Account/zone IDs are non-secret selectors.

Pinned CLI and MCP wrappers load the credential profile over inherited variables. Hosting API uses manifest account/zone selectors before profile selectors. CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID is optional and absent from the current all-domains profile.

If a zone selector is absent from the profile, an inherited CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID can still be a fallback. Inspect or unset it when switching project context.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/cloudflare-token.md).

<a id="environment-railway"></a>

## environment.railway

Railway workspace credentials, CI credentials, and target selectors.

Owner: **agents**.

Variable names: `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`, `RAILWAY_TOKEN`, `RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID`, `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID`, `RAILWAY_IAC_BRANCH`.

RAILWAY_API_TOKEN and RAILWAY_TOKEN are secret. IDs and branch names are selectors.

Workspace launchers clear inherited Railway tokens before loading the selected profile. RAILWAY_TOKEN is project/environment CI access; its value is maintained in the relevant CI secret store, not this registry.

Use one token type at a time and fail when the selected token is absent. Verify projectToken projectId/environmentId before CI secret replacement, and verify a PR plan afterward; never copy the local workspace credential to CI.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/railway.md).

GitHub CLI authentication and separate agent-connector account state.

Owner: **application**.

<a id="parallel-api-key"></a>

## parallel.api-key

Parallel API key for web search, extraction, and deep research, read from the shell secrets file.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `~/.secrets.sh`.

Variable names: `PARALLEL_API_KEY`.

Declared permissions: `Parallel account API access billed at API rates (Search, Extract, Task)`.

Consumers: skills/engineering-research/scripts/parallel.py and parallel-deep-research's API fallback, plus parallel-cli and the last30days engine when they inherit the shell environment.

parallel.py uses an inherited PARALLEL_API_KEY first; otherwise it reads only the literal assignment from ~/.secrets.sh (owner-only, mode 600, no expansions) and never executes the file. Never print the key.

Create or rotate the key at platform.parallel.ai, then replace only the PARALLEL_API_KEY assignment in ~/.secrets.sh, preserving other lines. Verify with a one-query parallel.py search; exit 3 means missing or rejected.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/configuration.md).

<a id="application-parallel-connectors"></a>

## application.parallel-connectors

Parallel connectors in the Codex and Claude apps, used only as an engineering-research fallback when its API script fails.

Owner: **application**.

Codex uses the Parallel app connector. Paul added the claude.ai Parallel connector on 2026-11-04; claude.ai offered no sign-in step, and its authentication and rate limits are not yet determined. claude.ai connectors also load in Claude Desktop and Claude Code sessions on the same account.

Connector grants are owned by each application account. Inventory does not inspect connector credentials.

engineering-research's scripts/parallel.py (search, full-page extract, deep research) uses the parallel.api-key credential and needs no connector or CLI.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/configuration.md).

Location: `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/settings.json`.

Keep the full native file and account state application-owned; export only deliberately managed preference keys.

Optional ~/.cursor/sandbox.json and ~/.cursor/permissions.json have different roles and schemas. Their absence does not determine effective UI/team policy. These surfaces are documented, not fully checked by agents-config.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/agent-customization.md).

<a id="application-cursor-auth"></a>

## application.cursor-auth

Cursor-managed account sign-in and per-client MCP authentication.

Owner: **application**.

Use supported Cursor account/MCP settings for sign-in and recovery. Native OAuth/credentials remain private and are not read by inventory checks.

The shared MCP JSON defines connections; a successful Codex/CLI connection does not establish authentication or available tools in Cursor. Verify each client against its intended account/resource.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/agent-customization.md).

<a id="environment-project-secrets"></a>

## environment.project-secrets

Application-local environment files and their runtime loaders.

Owner: **reference**.

Each project owns its .env, .env.local, or other declared environment-file locations and loader precedence. Inspect applicable project documentation and code; no global .env discovery or automatic loading by both agents is assumed.

The shell.secrets entry records ~/.secrets.sh; config/profiles.json owns registered provider-profile locations. Add per-project references and secret variable names when onboarding an app, never values, fragments, or hashes.

The user intends agents to make authorized environment/secret edits. Filesystem sandbox access, provider permission, and reload/redeploy behavior still need explicit capability checks in the selected harness.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/agent-customization.md).

## context.local-services

Existing local application/service ownership and lifecycle commands.

Owner: **reference**.

Location: `~/git/AGENTS.md`.

This external workspace document points to ~/git/local-dev/README.md and its service registry. It remains owned by those repositories; do not duplicate ports, routes, or process state here.

Use the owning manager and verify live PID/CWD/ownership/readiness before start/stop/kill. This registry entry is context, not a live service-health check.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/agent-customization.md).

<a id="twilio-sms-credentials"></a>

## twilio.sms-credentials

Private Twilio authentication and fixed sender/recipient for SMS to Paul.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `~/.agents/local/credentials/twilio-sms.env`.

Variable names: `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`, `TWILIO_TO_NUMBER`.

Consumers: `twilio.sms-cli`.

Required authentication is either TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN or the complete TWILIO_API_KEY_SID/TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET pair. agents-sms --check validates the active pair; generic inventory checks only the always-required names.

Initially copied only Twilio assignments from ~/git/paul/.env.local; existing authentication uses an account Auth Token. Source and copy are independently maintained. No values, phone numbers, or secret fragments belong in Git.

Ignored local profile must be owned by the current user, mode 600, in a mode-700 owner-owned directory. Stored numbers are private and not command arguments.

Existing provider grants were reused without rotation or scope expansion. Local checks are not provider authentication or delivery verification.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/sms.md).

<a id="twilio-sms-cli"></a>

## twilio.sms-cli

Dependency-free Node command for authorized SMS notifications to Paul's stored recipient.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `bin/agents-sms`.

Adapted from ~/git/paul/src/lib/sms.ts; maintained independently here. Requires Node >=22.18.0, local filesystem access, and outbound HTTPS to api.twilio.com.

Reads stdin or a file; --check and --dry-run are local only, --status reads one message. Sends at most four labeled requests, without automatic retries; successful submission is not final delivery.

No provider endpoint, MCP server, background automation, or native permission override is installed. Remote agents require separate authorized provisioning.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/sms.md).

<a id="application-last30days-config"></a>

## application.last30days-config

last30days engine settings, consent markers, and optional source keys on this machine.

Owner: **application**.

Location: `~/.config/last30days/.env`.

Created 2026-11-02 by the skill's first-run Auto setup from Claude Code. It holds the setup-complete, browser-consent, and X cookie-access-denied markers; no API keys were stored, and the engine never saves cookie values.

Paul granted browser-cookie consent in chat for X reads on that run and later runs. Set BROWSER_CONSENT=false or FROM_BROWSER=off in this file to revoke native browser and CDP reads.

Optional source keys (SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, X_BEARER_TOKEN) belong here or in macOS Keychain items named last30days-<KEY>. The engine also reads process-environment keys such as PARALLEL_API_KEY and PERPLEXITY_API_KEY. Derive key names only; never print the file.

The engine keeps run caches beside this file and saves research under ~/Documents/Last30Days. Setup installed yt-dlp with Homebrew; the Digg, arXiv, and Techmeme CLIs need Go and were not installed.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/last30days.md).

<a id="tool-claude-remote-shortcut"></a>

## tool.claude-remote-shortcut

cclaude shell function that runs one Remote Control server per folder.

Owner: **agents**.

Location: `scripts/claude-remote.py`.

~/.shortcuts.sh delegates cclaude to this helper. Preserve the rest of that external shell file; re-source it in existing terminals after changes.

Server mode (the default) brings back the folder's previous sessions within the roughly four-hour restore window and creates a session for each new app chat. --continue and --session-id select one session within that window, not a way to bypass it. Claude owns authentication and bridge-pointer state under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (normally ~/.claude); the helper reads the current directory record without modifying it.

Owner-only advisory locks live under ~/.agents/local/claude-remote. A live existing server in the folder is reported instead of taken over.

[Update and recovery instructions](../docs/runbooks/claude-remote.md).
